chunks: He said: 'As for whoever is wicked, We shall punish him, then he will be returned to his Lord, who will punish him with a strange punishment.'
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the two-stage punishment for the wicked in Surah Al-Kahf?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the dual nature of divine justice, where the 'strange punishment' (ʿadhāban nukran) signifies a unique severity reserved for those who transgressed against divine rights or the Imams. It reflects the belief that while worldly retribution may occur through historical events or the Ahl al-Bayt, the ultimate accountability remains with Allah, emphasizing the transition from temporal consequences to eternal, distinct retribution in the Hereafter.
